key_idea: Split trees into three structural cases. Embed almost all of the tree randomly so that leftover vertex and colour sets behave like independent random sets. Then finish with absorption-based matching or path lemmas that can use up exactly the colours that remain.
reason: The top-level structure is clear: random embedding, then a finishing step built on distributive absorption. But the argument rests on a long chain of technical lemmas, a three-way case split with a separate ad hoc Case C, and heavy parameter hierarchies with odd divisibility conditions such as 695|k. The main reason the result holds is visible, but it is buried under bookkeeping and probabilistic estimates rather than following from one clean idea.
recognized: Montgomery–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov, 'A proof of Ringel's Conjecture' (rainbow trees in ND-colourings of K_{2n+1})
